item.title: The Scream
item.medium: Oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard
item.lesson: Munch left us the event in his own words: walking at sunset along a road above Oslo's fjord, 'the sky suddenly turned blood-red... I stood there trembling with anxiety — and I sensed an infinite scream passing through nature.' Read that again: the figure on the bridge is not screaming — it is covering its ears against a scream coming from the world. The landscape carries the emotion: sky in bands of blood and fire, fjord dissolving into blue-black coils, while two unbothered companions walk on. Munch made four versions plus a lithograph; this 1893 painting in Oslo is the first. In 2021, infrared imaging confirmed that a faint pencil inscription on it — 'Can only have been painted by a madman' — was written by Munch himself, answering a critic who questioned his sanity. The image has since become the universal glyph of modern anxiety, reproduced to the point of comedy, which would not have surprised Munch: he knew he had painted something that belonged to everyone.
item.lookFor: Notice the railing's hard, straight diagonals — the only rigid lines in the picture. The built world stays geometric while nature liquefies; the figure is caught exactly between the two.
